observation.visible_scene: A night landscape over a calm, dark body of water. Across the middle of the frame runs a low, illuminated shoreline / industrial skyline (a band of white and orange lights with a thin vertical tower near the centre), and a dark silhouette of vegetation occupies the right edge. In the sky above the skyline a roughly horizontal row of six firework bursts (alternating white and orange, already fully expanded) hangs at a fixed height. A faint searchlight beam cuts diagonally up from the left side of the skyline. The water below mirrors the skyline lights, the searchlight, and the bursts as elongated, shimmering reflections.
visible_changes: The camera and the background skyline remain at fixed screen positions throughout the excerpt (no pan/zoom detected); the row of bursts keeps the same horizontal arrangement, so apparent motion is from the fireworks themselves, not the camera.
Over the segment the bursts drift slightly downward and gradually lose brightness / spread, while their reflections on the water shift shape and intensity due to surface ripples.

Thin vertical light streaks (rocket-trail-like lines) beneath several of the bursts, connecting them down toward the horizon, are faint/absent in the earliest frames and become clearly visible and persist through the later frames; their mirror images also appear in the water.
The left searchlight beam changes orientation and intensity, appearing as a faint diagonal line early and as a brighter, more vertical blue column on the left in later frames.
The bright band of shoreline lights and the central tower remain continuously lit; the right-side vegetation silhouette stays static.
outside_clip_unknowns: How and when the bursts were launched, and whether they were rising or just exploded before t=0 (the segment starts with them already expanded).
Whether the bursts continue to fall, fade, or vanish after the last frame, and whether new shells fire outside this window.
The exact cause of the vertical streaks becoming visible (exposure, falling sparks, or trails) is not determinable from the frames alone.
uncertain_details: The slow vertical displacement of the bursts is small and may be partly a fading/blur effect rather than true descent.
It is unclear whether the vertical streaks under the bursts are ascent trails, falling-spark streaks, or an exposure artefact; only their appearance over time is directly observable.
Water-surface 'motion' of the reflections is ripple-driven and does not indicate movement of the reflecting objects themselves.

Observe this actual video clip before reading any existing caption.
These are chronological samples of a TEMPORALLY CROPPED SEGMENT of a longer source video.
Both ends are arbitrary crop boundaries, not the beginning and completion of an action. Motion
may already be underway in the first view and may continue beyond the last. The endpoints need
NOT match or connect as a loop. Do not judge different endpoints as a physical inconsistency,
and do not invent a trigger, contact, start, stop, landing, disappearance or completion to make
the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.
If an editing cut is visible inside the segment, distinguish it from continuous physical motion;
do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.
Describe what is visible during the excerpt, the actual changes, and supported persistent
properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
occlusion, and an already ongoing process from its onset. Only state what the clip supports;
do not invent causes, an earlier impact, an unseen operator, material identities or later outcomes.
Do not infer motion from one frame, a visible seam or a single pose. Static intervals are valid.
Do not supply named physics laws. Compare each important entity's first and last image positions
and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
Return JSON {"visible_scene":"...", "visible_changes":["observation supported within the excerpt"],
"outside_clip_unknowns":["unseen prerequisites or outcomes, only when relevant"],
"uncertain_details":["..."]}. Be concrete and concise, in English. This is not a complete event reconstruction.
